﴿We reveal to them﴾ as We reveal to you, ﴿from among the people of the towns﴾, that is, the cities, not the people of the desert, because of the prevalence of harshness and cruelty among the Bedouins, and because the people of the cities are more complete in intellect, more perfect in forbearance, and more exalted in merit. ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ This refers to the polytheists who denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. That is: have these polytheists not traveled and looked upon the places of destruction of the past nations, so that they might take warning from them and cease from the denial they are engaged in? ﴿And the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾, that is, the Home of the Last Hour, or the state of the Hereafter, with the qualified noun omitted.

Al-Farra' said: the "Home" is the Hereafter itself, and a thing is attributed to itself because the wording differs, as in "the day of Friday," "the prayer of the first (Dhuhr)," and "the mosque of the congregation." The discussion of this is explained in the books of i'rab (grammatical analysis of the Qur'an).

By "this Home" is meant Paradise, that is: it is better for the God-fearing than the home of this world.

It was read as ﴿wa-la-dar al-Akhirah﴾ (with the lam of emphasis). Nafi', 'Asim and Ya'qub read ﴿Will you not then understand?﴾ with the ta' (second person, addressing them directly). The rest read it with the ya' (third person).

﴿Until, when the messengers despaired﴾: this clause of limit (ghayah) refers to an omitted element indicated by the context. Its estimated meaning is: "We did not send before you, O Muhammad, any but men, and We did not hasten punishment upon their nations who did not believe in what they brought, until, when the messengers despaired of victory through the punishment of their people." Or: "until, when the messengers despaired of the faith of their people because of their immersion in disbelief." ﴿And they thought that they had been denied﴾.

Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa', al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Rajā' al-Utaridi, 'Asim, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and Khalaf read ﴿kudhibū﴾ with the light (unstressed) form. The meaning is: the people thought that the messengers had lied to them about what they reported of the punishment, and that they had not been truthful. It was also said the meaning is: the people thought that the messengers had lied about their claim of victory over them. It was also said the meaning is: the messengers thought that their own selves had lied to them when they told them that they would be given victory over them, or that their hope of victory had deceived them.

The rest read ﴿kuddhibū﴾ with the doubled (stressed) form. The meaning in this reading is clear: the messengers thought that their people had denied them regarding what they had promised them of punishment. It is also permissible that the subject of "thought" is the people to whom the messengers were sent, in the sense that they thought the messengers had lied about what they brought of promise and threat.

Mujahid and Humayd read ﴿qad kadhabū﴾ with fatha on the kaf and dhal, lightly (unstressed), in the sense: "the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had lied." It has been said that thinking (zann) in this verse means certainty (yaqin), because the messengers were certain that their people had denied them, and this was not merely a supposition on their part. What should be said about interpreting "thinking" as "certainty" in a case like this is that it is interpreted by its original meaning in situations where there is merely supposition, as in the preceding examples.

﴿Our victory came to them﴾, that is, [p. 718] the victory of Allah, glory be to Him, came to the messengers suddenly, or the victory of Allah for His messengers came to the people of the messengers who denied them, by the sending of punishment upon the deniers.

﴿So whom We willed was saved﴾. 'Asim read ﴿fa-nujjiya﴾ with a single nun.

The rest read ﴿fa-nunjiya﴾ with two nuns. Abu Ubayd preferred the first reading, because it is written so in the Mushaf of 'Uthman.

Ibn Muhaysin read ﴿fa-naja﴾ in the active form. In the first reading, "man" (whom) is in the nominative position as the deputy subject; in the second reading it is in the accusative position as the object; and in the third reading it is in the nominative position as the subject. Those whom Allah saved are the messengers and those who believed with them, while the deniers were destroyed.

﴿And Our punishment is not averted from the criminal people﴾ when it descends upon them. In this is a statement that the one whom Allah wills to save from punishment is anyone other than these criminals.

﴿Certainly in their stories﴾, that is, the stories of the messengers and of the nations to whom they were sent, or in the story of Yusuf, his brothers and his father, ﴿is a lesson for those of understanding﴾. "Ibrah" (lesson) is reflection and insight that frees one from ignorance and bewilderment.

It has been said: it is a type of consideration (i'tibar), namely crossing from a known side to an unknown side. "Ulu al-albab" (those of understanding) are those of sound intellects who take lessons by their intellects and thus grasp what contains the interests of their religion. This story is a lesson because of what it includes of reports that correspond to reality, despite the long span of time between the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and the messengers whose stories are related, among whom are Yusuf, his brothers and his father, even though he (the Prophet) did not know their news and did not associate with their scholars.

﴿It is not a narration invented﴾, that is, this related matter, which is indicated by the mention of "stories," namely the Qur'an, which includes these things, is not a narration that is invented.

﴿But it is a confirmation of what was before it﴾, that is, the revealed books before it, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms. It was also read with the ﴿tasdiq﴾ in the nominative case, as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: it is a confirmation and an elaboration of every matter of the legislations that were stated briefly and need elaboration, because Allah, glory be to Him, did not neglect anything in the Book. It has also been said: the elaboration of every thing from the story of Yusuf with his brothers and father.

It has been said: the intended meaning is not its general implication, but rather the principles and rules and what they lead to. ﴿And guidance﴾ in this world, by which everyone whom Allah wills to guide is guided, ﴿and mercy﴾ in the Hereafter, by which Allah shows mercy to His servants who act upon what it contains, meeting the condition of true faith. For this reason He said: ﴿for a people who believe﴾, that is, who affirm it and what it includes of faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, His legislations and His decree. As for those other than them, they do not benefit from it, nor are they guided by the guidance it contains, so they do not deserve what those who believe deserve.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿We sent not before you any but men﴾: he said, that is, they were not from the people of heaven as you claimed.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah regarding the verse: he said, "We do not know that Allah ever sent a messenger except from the people of the towns, because they were more knowledgeable and more forbearing than the people of the wilderness."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan regarding His words ﴿how was the end of those before them﴾: he said, "How Allah punished the people of Nuh, the people of Lut, the people of Salih and the nations whom Allah punished."

Al-Bukhari and others narrated through the chain of 'Urwah that he asked Aisha about the words of Allah, glory be to Him, ﴿until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied﴾. He said: I said, "Were they denied, or were they denying (i.e., did the people deny them)?" meaning in this word, lightened or doubled. She said: "Rather they were denied," meaning with doubling. I said: "By Allah, they were certain that their people had denied them, so it is not a matter of supposition." She said: "Indeed, by my life, they were certain of that." I said: "Perhaps it is 'and they thought that they had been denied' with the lightened form?" She said: "God forbid! The messengers would never think that about their Lord." I said: "Then what is this verse?" She said: "They are the followers of the messengers who believed in them and affirmed them, and the trial lasted long upon them and the victory was delayed for them, until when the messengers despaired of those among their people who denied them, and the messengers thought that their followers had denied them, the victory of Allah came at that time."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah that Ibn Abbas recited to him ﴿and they thought that they had been denied﴾ in the lightened form, and said: "it means they were made to break their promise (ukhlifu)."

Ibn Abbas said: "They were human beings," and he recited ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him say, "When is the victory of Allah?"﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 214). Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: "'Urwah informed me from Aisha that she disagreed with that and refused it, and said: 'By Allah, Allah did not promise His messenger anything except that he knew it would occur before he died. But the trial continued upon the messengers until they thought that those who were with them of the believers had denied them.'" And she used to recite it with the doubled form.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the chain of 'Urwah from Aisha that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, recited ﴿and they thought that they had been denied﴾ in the lightened form.

Abu Ubayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through several chains from Ibn Abbas that he used to read "qad kudhibū" in the lightened form, and he said: "The messengers despaired of their people that they would respond to them, and their people thought that the messengers had lied to them about what they brought." ﴿Our victory came to them﴾: he said, "Our victory came to the messengers."

Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Tamim ibn Hadhlam who said: "I recited the Qur'an to Ibn Mas'ud and he did not correct me except for two letters: ﴿all came to Him humbled﴾ (An-Naml: 87), he said: 'atawhu' is lightened." And I recited to him "and they thought that they had been denied (kuddhibū)," and he said: "kudhibū" lightened. He said: "The messengers despaired of the faith of their people that they would believe in them, and their people, when the matter was delayed, thought that they had been denied."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the chain of Abu al-Ahwas from him, who said: "I memorized from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, in Surah Yusuf: ﴿and they thought that they had been denied﴾ lightened."

Regarding this matter, there is a statement from the earlier generations (al-salaf) that returns to what we have mentioned of the disagreement among the Companions.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿so whom We willed was saved﴾: he said, "So We save the messengers and whom We will." ﴿And Our punishment is not averted from the criminal people﴾. That is because Allah sent the messengers calling their peoples, and they informed them that whoever obeyed Allah would be saved, and whoever disobeyed Him would be punished and would go astray.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from him, who said: ﴿Their victory came to them﴾ is the punishment.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi: ﴿And Our punishment is not averted﴾, he said: "His punishment."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿Certainly in their stories﴾ [p. 719]: he said, "Yusuf and his brothers."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated ﴿a lesson for those of understanding﴾: he said, "well known to those of intellects."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah ﴿It is not a narration invented﴾: he said, "al-Firyah (invention) is lying." ﴿But it is a confirmation of what was before it﴾: he said, "The Qur'an confirms the books that were before it from the books of Allah which He revealed to His prophets, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms. It confirms all of them and bears witness that all of it is truth from Allah." ﴿And a detailed explanation of all things﴾: "Allah distinguished between His lawful and His unlawful, His obedience and His disobedience."
